data.note: Median of 12 Punjab mandis on 27 Nov (Rs5,075 per 40 kg; range TT Singh Rs4,100 to Chichawatni Rs5,650). Down 2.9% from 13,063 on 26 Nov (14 mandis); Okara-belt Sahiwal Rs4,860 and Pakpattan Rs5,300.

Dec-26 last traded $366.30 in the holiday-shortened 27 Nov session (market closed; Farmbucks snapshot 12:03 CT, not a confirmed settlement), +$4.70; Jan-27 $362.30. Week to 27 Nov +$25.30 (7.4%) from $341.00. Dec expires 14 Dec.

data.title: AMIS maize 28 Nov: belt median Rs6,700 per 100 kg on only four belt mandis; Sahiwal jumps to Rs6,650
data.summary: Okara Rs7,395, Kamalia Rs6,750, Sahiwal Rs6,650 (from Rs4,650) and Vehari Rs5,750 per 100 kg reported on 28 Nov; Pakpattan, Arifwala, Chichawatni, Burewala and Mailsi did not, so the +4.1% rise from Rs6,438 is partly a sample effect. Other Punjab median steady at Rs7,625 (7 mandis).

data.title: AMIS wheat 27 Nov: Punjab median eases 2.9% to Rs12,688 per 100 kg on 12 mandis
data.summary: Punjab wheat median fell to Rs5,075 per 40 kg (Rs12,688 per 100 kg) on 27 Nov from Rs13,063 on 26 Nov; range TT Singh Rs4,100 to Chichawatni Rs5,650 per 40 kg, Sahiwal Rs4,860.

data.title: CBOT 27 Nov: Dec soybean meal trades $366.30 (+$4.70), up $25.30 (7.4%) on the week
data.summary: In the shortened post-Thanksgiving session Dec meal last traded $366.30/st and Jan $362.30, extending the NOPA-led rally to a 7.4% weekly gain from $341.00 on 20 Nov (Farmbucks snapshot, not a confirmed settlement).

data.why: The belt median was Rs67.0/kg on 28 Nov but only four belt mandis reported (Okara, Kamalia, Sahiwal, Vehari), so the 4.1% rise from Rs64.4/kg on 26 Nov partly reflects the cheaper Pakpattan, Burewala and Mailsi rows dropping out; Sahiwal also moved from Rs46.5 to Rs66.5/kg. It is 9.4% above 28 Oct (Rs61.3/kg), 15.3% below a year ago (Rs79.1/kg on 28 Nov 2025) and at 45% of its 52-week range (Rs54.4–82.5/kg); other Punjab mandis hold at a Rs76.3/kg median, so the belt is still the cheapest source while autumn-crop arrivals peak in Nov–Dec.
data.act: Keep buying dry new-crop in weekly lots, Vehari first (Rs57.5/kg on 28 Nov), then Sahiwal (Rs66.5/kg) and Kamalia (Rs67.5/kg); Okara is Rs74.0/kg. Ask Pakpattan, Burewala and Mailsi traders for fresh quotes since those mandis did not report. Reject lots above 14% moisture or failing aflatoxin.

data.why: CBOT Dec soybean meal last traded $366.30/st on 27 Nov, up $4.70 on the day and $25.30 (7.4%) on the week, with Jan at $362.30, after NOPA's low meal yield and fresh Chinese buying. Pakistan still buys meal from local crushers only: import approvals were deferred on 23 Oct and current GM soybean licences run only through November 2026, with no renewal found as of 28 Nov.
data.act: Lock Dec–Jan needs before 30 Nov with at least two crushers holding bean stocks, before they reprice to a CBOT meal price now above $365/st; a licence lapse at end-November would tighten local supply further.
